quotes.text: The problem isn't that it can't handle your data. It's that it always assumes you'll have ten times more of it later.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Think of fusion teams as your test lab. You prove the concept cheaply, validate value quickly, and migrate after success, not before it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The metric worth worshiping isn't scale or architecture. Its turnaround time. The shorter the loop between idea and implementation, the healthier the system.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names a concrete success metric for business apps.

takeaways: Model-driven Power Apps depend on Dataverse, which brings licensing, environments, security roles and governance overhead that many simple business apps never need.
A fusion team can deliver most of the value with SharePoint lists for data, Power Automate for approvals and notifications, and Teams as the interface.
Start light, prove value quickly and move to Dataverse only when real requirements such as complex integrations or regulated data demand it.
hook: Model-driven Power Apps sound enterprise-ready, but for many teams they turn a simple tracker into a Dataverse project full of security roles, environments and change requests. This episode shows makers and IT leads when to skip Dataverse and build faster with a fusion team using Teams, SharePoint lists and Power Automate.
